exact_subject: Specialize foreign downcalls from runtime-compiled Truffle code
summary: One confirmed portable test defect: labs is incorrectly assumed to use 64-bit C long on Windows x64. No production semantic defect proven by this source review. Native-image execution and several semantic requirements remain unverified.

findings.title: Use a portable 64-bit C function in the long downcall test
findings.detail: The test binds labs to a (JAVA_LONG)->JAVA_LONG descriptor and requires labs(-(1L << 40)) to return 1L << 40. Windows x64 uses LLP64: C long and labs arguments/results are 32 bits. The low 32 bits of this input are zero, so the assertion cannot succeed. The new native Truffle gate registers this test without an OS exclusion, and ForeignFunctions supports Win64. This is a test ABI defect, independent of the new linker implementation.
findings.evidence: ffm-first-artifacts/labs-abi-probe.c, labs-win64.s and labs-linux64.s: cross-compiled static assertions verify C long widths; optimized Windows probe returns 0 while Linux returns 1099511627776.
findings.fix: Use llabs with JAVA_LONG for the fixed 64-bit case, or derive the C long layout from Linker.canonicalLayouts and keep a separate portable 64-bit test.
findings.validation_limit: Windows C ABI cross-compilation and source trace, not Windows native-image execution.
